title: Fibonacci EA v5.0 H1 Timeframe Transition Test
research_question: Does transitioning execution from M30 to H1 further filter candlestick noise, improve trade win-rate and payoff, and maintain profitability on GBPUSD without reducing trade sample size to statistically invalid levels?
hypothesis: Executing entry signals on H1 candles eliminates intraday lower-timeframe noise and aligns execution directly with swing lookback structure, achieving low drawdown and high win rate, but may significantly reduce trade frequency compared to M30.

facts: EXP-0018 on M30 achieved Profit Factor 3.44 and 2.35% drawdown in training (2020-2024) across 16 trades.
EXP-0019 on M30 achieved +$163.34 profit, Profit Factor 1.13, and 3.88% drawdown in validation (2025) across 87 trades.
The EA detects swings on H1 bars (CopyHigh/Low on PERIOD_H1), making H1 execution completely synchronous with swing detection.
inferences: Executing on H1 bars will produce even cleaner candlestick rejection signals.
Trade frequency on H1 may drop considerably compared to M30, testing the lower boundary of sample size sufficiency.
evidence: EXP-0018 total_trades=16, profit_factor=3.44, win_rate=81.25%, total_net_profit=531.64, equity_drawdown_maximal_percent=2.35
EXP-0019 total_trades=87, profit_factor=1.13, win_rate=78.16%, total_net_profit=163.34, equity_drawdown_maximal_percent=3.88

independent_variables.name: timeframe
independent_variables.rationale: Transition execution chart timeframe from M30 to H1 to test higher timeframe noise reduction and synchronous swing detection.

assumptions: EA logic functions correctly when executed on H1 timeframe.
H1 bars provide valid rejection wicks and Fibonacci touch signals without breaking execution timers.
expected_observations: Total net profit remains positive on GBPUSD.
falsification_conditions: Total net profit <= 0.0 on training or validation partition.
